In the vCPU-run asm blob
column2: the guest's RCX is temporarily saved onto the

column1: stack after VM-Exit as the exit flow must first load a register with a
pointer to the vCPU's save area in order to save the guest's registers.
RCX is arbitrarily designated as the scratch register.
Since the stack usage is to (1)save host
and (4)load guest
column2: the code can't conform to the stack's natural FIFO

column1: semantics
column2: i.e. it can't simply do PUSH/POP.  Regardless of whether it

column1: is done for the host's value or guest's value
needs to access the stack using a non-traditional method
instead of POP.  vCPU-run opts to create a placeholder on the stack for
guest's RCX (by adjusting RSP) and saves RCX to its place immediately
after VM-Exit (via MOV).
In other words
column2: the purpose of the first 'PUSH RCX' at the start of

column1: the vCPU-run asm blob  is to adjust RSP down
actually access memory.  Use 'SUB $wordsize
to make it more obvious that the intent is simply to create a gap on
the stack for the guest's RCX.
